title: improv·artist · ghostly (Doris Salcedo)
mutation_directive: improv artist: ghostly via Doris Salcedo

improv_extras.practice: absence as form; furniture filled with concrete; political hush

v1.feedback: The Salcedo concept lands well — concrete/ash/bone palette is restrained and appropriate, and the top-down erosion with ash-fall drift genuinely channels 'absence as form' rather than just being a visual gimmick. However, using the LeePerrySmith head as the base geometry is a missed opportunity: Salcedo's work is about furniture, domestic objects, architectural voids — a chair or table silhouette filled with particles would be far more conceptually precise. The erosion cycle could benefit from longer stillness before crumbling begins, letting the 'political hush' breathe; right now the 4-second reveal into erosion feels rushed for the weight this piece wants to carry. Consider scaling up the point size slightly and pulling the camera in — at default distance the form reads but doesn't command the frame the way Salcedo's installations dominate a room.

v2.feedback: The Salcedo mapping is legible — concrete/ash/bone palette, interior-fill particles, and the ash-settling reveal all serve the brief well. The top-down erosion cycling with presence/absence is a smart read of 'political hush.' Two things hold it back: the box-constructed chair is too geometrically clean — Salcedo's furniture carries material weight and wear, so rounding corners or warping vertices with low-frequency noise would sell the heaviness better. Second, 65k particles with additive blending on muted grays risk reading as a dim, low-contrast ghost rather than a dense concrete mass — either boost particle count to ~120k or mix in a small proportion of opaque (non-additive) core particles so the seat and legs feel solid while the edges dissolve.
